scenes.heading: Solving equations by backtracking
scenes.sub: Work backwards to find the starting number
scenes.say: If you know where you ended up and every step you took, you can always find where you started. That's the idea behind backtracking.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Socks on, then shoes. Take shoes off first, then socks.
scenes.science: The last operation done to x is the first one you undo
scenes.breaks: with clothes you just take things off; in maths each operation has its own opposite that you must choose.
scenes.say: You put your socks on, then your shoes. At night you take your shoes off first, then your socks. Backtracking is the same: the last thing done to x is the first thing you undo.

scenes.heading: Inverse operations
scenes.say: Each operation has an inverse that undoes it. Adding is undone by subtracting, and multiplying is undone by dividing. These pairs are partners.

scenes.heading: How to backtrack
steps: Start at the answer on the right
scenes.say: First, build a flowchart from x using the order of operations. Then start at the answer and work backwards, undoing the last operation first. Finally, check your answer.

scenes.heading: Build it, then undo it
scenes.say: First we build the flowchart for two x plus three equals seventeen: start with x, times two, then plus three, to get seventeen. Now undo it from the right: seventeen minus three is fourteen, and fourteen divided by two is seven. So x equals seven.
scenes.caption: 2x + 3 = 17: 17 − 3 = 14, 14 ÷ 2 = 7, so x = 7

scenes.heading: Worked example
scenes.question: Solve 3x + 5 = 26.
scenes.say: Solve three x plus five equals twenty-six. The flowchart is times three, then plus five. Undo plus five: twenty-six minus five is twenty-one. Undo times three: twenty-one divided by three is seven. So x equals seven.
scenes.caption: Solve 3x + 5 = 26. The flowchart is × 3, then + 5. Undo + 5: 26 − 5 = 21. Undo × 3: 21 ÷ 3 = 7. So x = 7.

scenes.heading: Brackets go first
scenes.question: Solve 2(x + 6) = 30.
scenes.say: With brackets, the inside happens first. For two lots of x plus six equals thirty, the flowchart is plus six, then times two. So undo times two first: fifteen. Then subtract six: x equals nine.
scenes.caption: With brackets, the inside happens first. For 2(x + 6) = 30, the flowchart is + 6, then × 2. So undo × 2 first: 15. Then subtract 6: x = 9.

scenes.say: Quick recap. Use inverse operations, undo the last step first, and always check by substituting. Now try the practice questions!
